# [CS073] Unused Function (dead-code)

A function is unreachable from the program's entry points.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | LOW |
| **Category** | Code Metrics |
| **CWE** | - |
| **OWASP** | - |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Unused functions still have to be read, maintained and kept secure. Reachability is computed on the call graph from main, init, tests and exported API.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func legacyExport() { /* no callers */ }
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
// remove the function, or call it where it is needed
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [dead-code]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    dead-code: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore dead-code -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** dead-code
```
